subject: english-language-arts
title: Launch and diagnostic: strongest textual evidence
essential_question: How can understanding evidence, independence, and academic conversation help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about strongest textual evidence, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of strongest textual evidence.
Check, revise, or improve work about strongest textual evidence using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about strongest textual evidence.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “strongest textual evidence.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Read or listen closely, annotate or notice craft, discuss evidence, and create a written or spoken response for a real purpose. Keep the explanation centered on strongest textual evidence. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about strongest textual evidence. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of strongest textual evidence and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about strongest textual evidence; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of strongest textual evidence and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about strongest textual evidence; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for strongest textual evidence, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for strongest textual evidence works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of strongest textual evidence, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking strongest textual evidence mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use annotations, discussion notes, reading response, writing sample, revision, and transfer to a new text; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply strongest textual evidence under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting strongest textual evidence.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

essential_question: How can understanding poetry, style, and rhetorical language help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Apply tone shifts independently in a new representation, text, situation, or design constraint.

materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “tone shifts.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Read or listen closely, annotate or notice craft, discuss evidence, and create a written or spoken response for a real purpose. Keep the explanation centered on tone shifts. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about tone shifts. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of tone shifts and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about tone shifts; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of tone shifts and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about tone shifts; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for tone shifts, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for tone shifts works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of tone shifts, and avoid unnecessary remediation.

materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “research limits and ethics.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Read or listen closely, annotate or notice craft, discuss evidence, and create a written or spoken response for a real purpose. Keep the explanation centered on research limits and ethics. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about research limits and ethics. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of research limits and ethics and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about research limits and ethics; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of research limits and ethics and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about research limits and ethics; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for research limits and ethics, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for research limits and ethics works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of research limits and ethics, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking research limits and ethics mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use annotations, discussion notes, reading response, writing sample, revision, and transfer to a new text; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply research limits and ethics under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.

essential_question: How can understanding publication, portfolio, and transition capstone help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for presentation and defense, then demonstrate corrected understanding.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of presentation and defense.
Check, revise, or improve work about presentation and defense using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about presentation and defense.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “presentation and defense.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Read or listen closely, annotate or notice craft, discuss evidence, and create a written or spoken response for a real purpose. Keep the explanation centered on presentation and defense. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about presentation and defense. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of presentation and defense and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about presentation and defense; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of presentation and defense and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about presentation and defense; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for presentation and defense, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for presentation and defense works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of presentation and defense, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking presentation and defense mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use annotations, discussion notes, reading response, writing sample, revision, and transfer to a new text; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply presentation and defense under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting presentation and defense.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of presentation and defense in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
